Let  

\[
A=(0,0),\qquad B=(b,0),\qquad C=(0,c)
\]

so that \(\triangle ABC\) is right–angled at \(A\) and  

\[
b^2+c^2=BC^2=38^2=1444. \tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Coordinates of \(K\) and \(L\)

For \(K\) we have  

\[
AK=BK=14\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\begin{cases}
x_K^2+y_K^2=196,\\
(x_K-b)^2+y_K^2=196.
\end{cases}
\]

Subtracting gives \(x_K=b/2\).  
Hence  

\[
y_K^2=196-\frac{b^2}{4}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
K=\Bigl(\frac{b}{2},\,\sqrt{196-\frac{b^2}{4}}\Bigr). \tag{2}
\]

Similarly for \(L\),

\[
AL=CL=14\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\begin{cases}
x_L^2+y_L^2=196,\\
x_L^2+(y_L-c)^2=196,
\end{cases}
\]

which gives \(y_L=c/2\) and  

\[
x_L^2=196-\frac{c^2}{4}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
L=\Bigl(\sqrt{196-\frac{c^2}{4}},\,\frac{c}{2}\Bigr). \tag{3}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Using \(KL=14\)

The condition \(KL=14\) gives

\[
\Bigl(\frac{b}{2}-\sqrt{196-\frac{c^2}{4}}\Bigr)^2
+\Bigl(\sqrt{196-\frac{b^2}{4}}-\frac{c}{2}\Bigr)^2=196.
\]

After expanding and simplifying, this reduces to  

\[
c\sqrt{196-\frac{b^2}{4}}
+b\sqrt{196-\frac{c^2}{4}}=196. \tag{4}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Solving for \(b\) and \(c\)

Let \(a=b^2,\; d=c^2\).  
Equation (4) becomes  

\[
c\sqrt{196-\frac{a}{4}}
+b\sqrt{196-\frac{d}{4}}=196.
\]

Squaring and using \(a+d=1444\) from (1) yields the quadratic

\[
a^2-1444a+519\,168=0,
\]

whose solutions are \(a=768,\; d=676\) (or vice‑versa).  
Thus

\[
b^2=768,\qquad c^2=676
\]
\[
\boxed{\,b=16\sqrt3,\; c=26\,}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Coordinates of the points

\[
\begin{aligned}
B&=(16\sqrt3,\,0),\\
C&=(0,\,26),\\
K&=\Bigl(\frac{b}{2},\,\sqrt{196-\frac{b^2}{4}}\Bigr)
   =\Bigl(8\sqrt3,\,2\Bigr),\\
L&=\Bigl(\sqrt{196-\frac{c^2}{4}},\,\frac{c}{2}\Bigr)
   =\Bigl(3\sqrt3,\,13\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5.  Area of quadrilateral \(BKLC\)

Using the shoelace formula for the vertices in order  
\(B\to K\to L\to C\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sum}_1 &= (16\sqrt3)(2)+(8\sqrt3)(13)+(3\sqrt3)(26)=214\sqrt3,\\
\text{Sum}_2 &= 0\cdot(8\sqrt3)+2\cdot(3\sqrt3)+13\cdot0+26\cdot(16\sqrt3)=422\sqrt3.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence

\[
\text{Area}=\frac12\bigl|\text{Sum}_1-\text{Sum}_2\bigr|
          =\frac12\bigl|214\sqrt3-422\sqrt3\bigr|
          =\frac12(208\sqrt3)=104\sqrt3.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
The area of \(BKLC\) is \(104\sqrt3\), so \(n=104\).

\[
\boxed{104}
\]
